title: The dialect written on social media

blocks.text: Today most of the written dialect no longer uses Arabic, but Arabic characters: posts, comments, captions, transcribed voice messages. The dialect in Arabic does not have an official spelling: everyone writes as pronunciation, with different graphs for the same word, elongated letters, forgotten hamza, fuṣḥā and Egyptian mixed in the same sentence. For those who work on open sources it is a valuable material (that's where you read people's reactions) and difficult (search engines don't recognize variants). In this unit learn the graphic conventions of the written Egyptian, the spy-words of the Levant and the Gulf on social media, the language of comments (irony, emoji, hashtag) and a method to read a thread separating news, opinions and vowels. Unit of Understanding . Five weeks, in parallel with INT-04INT-05 and the Test B2.2.

rows: ARZ-01; EGY-11 EGY-15; B2-12; INT-05 (in parallel)
7–8 hours · five weeks (weeks 204–208), about 1,5 hours per week

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. recognize the most frequent Egyptian spells written in Arabic characters and link them to pronunciation;
2. recognize the spy words of the Levant and the Gulf in the comments;
3. understand the language of comments: stretches, emoji, hashtag, irony, switching with the fuṣḥā;
4. read a thread of comments and classify their content (news, opinion, voice, joke);
5. summarize in English, with the powers, the reactions of social media to a news.
Five-week plan (a block from 60 minutes and one by 30 per week).

chapters.title: 3. Levante and Gulf on social media

blocks.text: ⁧ما فيما في⁩ (Iraq) ⁧ماكو⁩ · ⁧مافيش⁩ There isn't

The spy words. ⁧شو⁩ , ⁧هيك⁩ , ⁧بدي⁩ , ⁧عم⁩ → almost certainly Levantine; ⁧شلون⁩ , ⁧وايد⁩ , ⁧الحين⁩ , ⁧زين⁩ → Gulf (and Iraq); ⁧ده⁩ , ⁧عايز⁩ , ⁧مش⁩ , ⁧كده⁩ → Egypt. Like the Arabic, it's a clue, not proof.

Reading aloud helps. The written dialect is phonetic: reading it aloud with the Egyptian pronunciation (EGY), words like ⁧اوي⁩ , ⁧تلاتة⁩ , ⁧ده⁩ they become immediately clear. Read the guided messages with the tutor, then alone, at increasing speed. The elongated letters are read by lengthening the vowel, not repeating the consonant: ⁧بعيييد⁩ = bʿīīīd, ⁧سلااام⁩ = salāāām.
